newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia plans major diplomatic cuts.
newsitem.headline: Australia plans major diplomatic cuts.

text.p: The Australian Foreign Affairs and Trade Department faces the loss of 225 jobs and the scaling down of some diplomatic posts under a draft restructuring plan released on Thursday.
The plan outlined total government savings of A$28 million (US$20 million) over the 1997/98 and 1998/99 financial years, a department spokesman told Reuters.
"The draft plan of action sets out a blueprint for a reinvigorated and reshaped (department)..." the spokesman said.
A total of 270 staff accepted voluntary redundancy in the year to June 30, 1997 and 130 others have expressed an interest in a voluntary redundancy in the past three weeks.
The department has targeted 225 voluntary redundancies in the year to June 1998, bringing staff numbers down to 2,100 from 2,500 in mid-1995.
"There has been continuing budget pressure on this department and everyone else in Canberra for the last two years or more and that has led to a downsizing in the last year," the spokesman said.
Australia's 16-month-old conservative government has slashed spending in all areas, except defence, in a bid to return its budget to a surplus.
